A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe VIRES and VIRESET. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix Sections 7.1–7.5 are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations, and user studies in Section 5 and Table 1, plus architecture, conditioning, and sparsity experiments in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark and user-study outcomes and appendix experiments in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: The Open-Sora-based framework, Sequential ControlNet, standardized self-scaling, sketch attention, sketch-aware encoder, losses, and application procedures are unchanged. Table 2 changes architecture labels, not their layer specifications.

E1.justification: Both versions use VIRESET and DAVIS and retain the same repainting, replacement, generation, removal, inpainting, sparse-sketch, and long-video scenarios. Appendix experiments with edge and depth conditioning are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Both versions compare against Rerender, VidToMe, Text2Video-Zero, RAVE, and VideoComposer in Table 1. The VideoComposer comparison for sketch-to-video generation and inpainting in Figure 9 and all ablation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The training budgets, preprocessing, 51-frame video settings, five quantitative metrics, and selection of 50 evaluation videos per dataset are unchanged. User studies retain 10 samples per dataset and 25 volunteers; appendix training and testing protocols also match.

E4.justification: Both retain the four component ablations, Sequential ControlNet architecture comparison, self-scaling analysis under edge/depth conditioning, and sketch-sparsity sensitivity analysis. The supplementary qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Participant counts and independent-evaluation reporting in the user studies remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1 and 3–5 and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains VIRES PSNR values of 23.87 on VIRESET and 25.36 on DAVIS, with the same comparator scores and rankings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and their accompanying mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged, including flow matching, latent masking, feature scaling, sketch attention, and training losses. No formal assumptions or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same method, dataset, application, novelty, and comparative-performance claims. The revised title does not change their scientific meaning or scope.

C2.justification: The component interpretations, explanation of stronger self-scaling benefits for edge maps than depth maps, and potential backbone compatibility are unchanged. Both retain the computational limitation of approximately 323 seconds per 51-frame video on an A6000 GPU.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link at the end of the abstract, providing an additional access pointer. The PDFs do not establish a new code or data release; preprocessing instructions, hardware, training hyperparameters, and the pretrained-model link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 53 references and substantive positioning relative to prior work are retained. Reference 20 changes only its citation-location page number after text reflow.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'with Sketch and Text Guidance' to 'via Sketch and Text Guided Generation,' and affiliations and author footnotes are revised. The main prose, section sequence, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Front-matter changes reflow material on pages 1–3. Table 2 replaces 'Ours (VIRES)' and the three variation names with headers '1–4,' while Table 3 retains the original names. Figure content and the remaining table displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly connects Table 2 architectures to the named results in Table 3. v3 replaces those architecture names with unexplained numbers while Table 3 retains the names in a different order, making architecture-to-result matching harder. The added project-page pointer is a modest access aid, but the revision introduces a concrete loss of technical clarity while leaving the scientific evidence unchanged.
